one_liner: C11 x86/x86-64 decoder, formatter and encoder with no allocation; decode+format 1.2-1.35x Capstone's throughput in disas-bench.
what_it_does: Zydis decodes x86 and x86-64 machine code (16/32/64-bit modes, AVX-512, AMX and APX encodings) into a ZydisDecodedInstruction plus an operand array. It formats instructions as Intel, Intel MASM or AT&T text through a formatter with 74 hookable callbacks, and since v4 it also encodes instructions. The v4 API splits decoding into ZydisDecoderDecodeInstruction and an optional ZydisDecoderDecodeOperands call, so callers pay only for the operands they ask for. ZydisDecoderEnableMode(ZYDIS_DECODER_MODE_MINIMAL) returns only length, mnemonic, operand and address size and raw fields. The API is unrelated to Capstone's cs_disasm_iter, so switching means rewriting call sites.
how_it_is_fast: Decoding walks a generated decoder tree of 16-bit nodes (src/Generated/DecoderTables.inc, built from the zydis-db instruction definitions). ZydisDecodeInstruction switches on the node type (opcode, mode, ModRM mod/reg/rm, mandatory prefix, operand size, REX.W, vector length, EVEX/MVEX bits) until it reaches a definition leaf, so there is no pattern matching and no allocation. Work is opt-in: operand decoding is a separate call limited to the operand count you pass, and minimal mode skips semantic analysis (1.8x the full decode-only throughput in disas-bench, derived from page data). Unlike Capstone, which always produces text, Zydis can stop after decoding.
when_to_use: C or C++ disassemblers, debuggers and JIT inspectors that print x86-64 code: in disas-bench decode+format, Zydis v4.1.0 ran 33.3 MB/s vs Capstone 27.5 MB/s (Ryzen 9 9950X) and 35.0 vs 25.9 MB/s (i9-13900K), and 1.6-1.8x Intel XED's decode+format rate.
Tools that both decode and re-encode x86 (binary rewriting, instrumentation, code generation): Zydis ships an encoder in the same library, with zasm as an asmjit-style C++ front-end.

Kernel drivers, UEFI and other freestanding code: no malloc, a no-libc build (ZYAN_NO_LIBC) and Zycore as the only dependency, tested on Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, Linux and UEFI in user and kernel mode.
Length decoding and mnemonic scans over large code: minimal mode reached 90-103 MB/s decode-only in disas-bench, about 1.8x the full decode.
Output that must match a particular assembler syntax or be post-processed: Intel, MASM and AT&T styles plus per-token formatter hooks.
when_not_to_use: Raw throughput when Rust or .NET is acceptable: in the same disas-bench charts, iced (160-165 MB/s) and yaxpeax-x86 (192-197 MB/s) decode+format about 4.7-5.9x faster than Zydis, and diStorm3 2.7-3.0x faster.
Decode-only work where XED or bddisasm already fit: Zydis full decode (50-57 MB/s) is slower than XED (67-73) and bddisasm (103-106) in the same runs.
Storing decoded instructions in bulk: a full decode is about 1.1 KB (ZydisDecodedInstruction plus 10 ZydisDecodedOperand, issue #554, open), against roughly 40 bytes for iced; copy out what you need.
Non-x86 targets or multi-architecture tools: Zydis decodes x86/x86-64 only, while Capstone covers ARM, MIPS, RISC-V and others.

Tracking master: master is the unreleased 5.0.0 (project(Zydis VERSION 5.0.0.0)); the README says API stability is guaranteed only at tagged commits and ABI stability only between patch versions. The latest release is v4.1.1 (2025-02-16).

integration.form: static lib (shared optional via ZYDIS_BUILD_SHARED_LIB; amalgamated single header plus single source in each release)
integration.dependencies: Zycore (zyantific's own C support library, git submodule or system package); no third-party dependencies, libc optional
integration.min_toolchain: C11 (C_STANDARD 11 via zyan_set_common_flags; MSVC builds without forcing a standard), CMake 3.10+; Visual Studio 2022 project and Meson build also provided
integration.platforms: Decodes x86 and x86-64 code (16/32/64-bit modes). Host: any platform with a C11 compiler; tested on Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, Linux and UEFI, user and kernel mode. Packages in Debian, Ubuntu, Arch, Homebrew, NixOS and vcpkg.
integration.thread_safety: Thread-safe by design per the README: no global mutable state and no allocation; ZydisDecoder and ZydisFormatter are read-only during decode and format, and each thread uses its own instruction, context and operand buffers.

gotchas: Harness note (does not inflate Zydis): disas-bench passes ZYDIS_MAX_OPERAND_COUNT_VISIBLE (5) to ZydisDecoderDecodeOperands, which clamps to instruction.operand_count, a count that includes hidden operands. So the full rows also decode implicit operands such as RSP and stack memory that the formatter never prints; the maintainers recommend operand_count_visible (issue #554). Each tool is timed once (clock() over 20 passes of the 0x2460400-byte .text of a Firefox xul.dll) with no variance, chart values are read off PNGs, and the suite belongs to Joel Hoener (athre0z), a Zydis copyright holder. The 2021 icedland/disas-bench run by the iced author (i5-6600K, gcc 10.3) independently put Zydis at 22.24 vs Capstone 14.02 MB/s decode+format (1.59x, derived from page data).

The measured build is the v4.1.0 tag (submodule 569320a, 2024-02-04). Master has since added formatter speedups (20d64cb hex digit count, 8a6cdb0 early prefix skip, July 2026) and a decoder-tree reorder (PR #638, 78,397 to 67,585 table elements). PR #638 also fixed REX2 instructions with a mandatory 66 prefix and changed 66 0F 1E/0F 1B NOP decoding. None of these is on the hot path of the measured legacy 64-bit code, so the numbers stand for v4.1.0, but master's speed is unmeasured.

Default decoder modes reinterpret legacy encodings: MPX, CET, LZCNT, TZCNT, CLDEMOTE, IPREFETCH and APX are on by default. F3 0F BD decodes as lzcnt rather than bsr, wide NOPs decode as MPX or CET instructions, and with APX mode 0xD5 is a REX2 prefix. Enabling KNC mode disables all AVX-512 decoding. Open issue #539: 0f 1a de decodes as 'nop ebx' and drops the esi operand (XED gives 'nop esi, ebx').

The README example's ZydisDisassembleIntel/ATT re-initialises the decoder and formatter and decodes every operand on each call; its header says to call the separate decode and format functions if performance matters. CVE-2021-41253 (heap corruption from an uninitialised formatter buffer string, reachable only from custom formatter hooks) was fixed in v3.2.1.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Zydis over Capstone and Intel XED when you print x86-64 from C or C++ and also want an encoder, AT&T/MASM/Intel styles with formatter hooks, or a no-libc kernel/UEFI build; it formats faster than both in disas-bench. Pick bddisasm for richer per-instruction semantics at similar or better decode+format speed (46.8 vs 33.3 MB/s on the 9950X, about equal on the i9-13900K), diStorm3 for 2.7-3x the decode+format rate in plain C, and iced or yaxpeax-x86 when raw speed matters most and Rust or .NET is acceptable.
verified_claims_summary: In athre0z/disas-bench, each harness linearly sweeps the 0x2460400-byte .text of a checked-in Firefox xul.dll 20 times. Zydis v4.1.0 (CMake Release, decode plus up to 5 operands plus Intel formatting) is compared with Capstone 5.0.6 (Makefile -O3, x86 only, cs_disasm_iter with detail off, which always formats). Decode+format: 33.3 vs 27.5 MB/s on a Ryzen 9 9950X (Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3) and 35.0 vs 25.9 MB/s on an i9-13900K (Debian trixie, GCC 14.2), 1.21x and 1.35x (derived from page data, chart readings). The record's hardware field (i5-6600K, Kubuntu 21.04) belongs to the 2021 icedland fork, not to these charts.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-07-27 on the unreleased 5.0.0 master; latest release v4.1.1, 2025-02-16), MIT-licensed, fuzzed on OSS-Fuzz, packaged by major distributions and shipped inside x64dbg, Firefox and WebKit, so it is low-risk to adopt; vendor the amalgamated release files or a tagged commit, not master.
